inspection_summary: Complete line-by-line inspection found a coherent computational account: historical certification by zero counts and critical-line sign changes, replacement of Euler-Maclaurin work by the shorter Riemann-Siegel expansion, an error-aware SWAC screening and refinement pipeline, a census of structured Gram-law failures, fine-mesh resolution of near-coincident zeros, and an explicitly informal interpretation of delicate term cancellation. Formula typography is OCR-risky but the main mechanisms are recoverable from prose; the plotted curves in both figures are not recoverable from the text layer.

accepted_units.title: Finite critical-line verification as a bounded computational claim
accepted_units.why_material: The paper sharply separates a finite numerical result from the unrestricted hypothesis: the first 10,000 zeros are reported simple and on the critical line, yielding verification only through a stated height.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the declared purpose, prior-work relation, numerical extent, bounded RH conclusion, and machine-time feasibility claim.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The zeta-series display and critical-line notation are OCR-degraded, but the scope and conclusion are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Gram intervals, Gram's law, and adjacent compensation
accepted_units.why_material: This span defines the interval-based prediction used to organize the search, states why universal validity would imply RH, and immediately shows that individual failures can be locally compensated by double-root neighboring intervals.
accepted_units.context_note: Kept through the first concrete paired failures so the law is not detached from its known limitation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The defining equation and symbols are OCR-risky; the interval construction, one-root prediction, and failure pattern are recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: Global zero count plus critical-line sign changes
accepted_units.why_material: Hutchinson's strategy combines an independent count of all zeros in a rectangle with at least as many critical-line roots detected by sign changes, excluding off-line zeros in the bounded region; the span also identifies the term-count bottleneck of the Euler-Maclaurin implementation.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the rectangular count, the logical comparison, the expansion used, and the reason desk-calculator computation became prohibitive.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula details and subscripts are damaged, so reuse should rely on the checked prose mechanism unless the scan is consulted.

accepted_units.title: Riemann-Siegel compression of critical-line evaluation
accepted_units.why_material: The source contrasts the earlier order-of-t workload with an expansion requiring only about the square root of the height in terms, then links that reduction to a substantially larger verified range and an explicit count of Gram-law failures.
accepted_units.context_note: The auxiliary real function, phase, expansion, remainder estimate, punched-card computation, and resulting verification are kept together.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed formulas are substantially OCR-corrupted; the term-count comparison, reality of the transformed function, approximate remainder scale, and reported outcome are clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Machine access as a boundary on numerical evidence
accepted_units.why_material: Aborted differential-analyzer and ENIAC plans, followed by Turing's bounded Manchester runs, show that the extent and continuity of verification depended materially on available computing architecture and time rather than only on mathematical formulas.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both unrealized routes and the two completed but incomplete Manchester computations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: No essential dependency beyond mildly degraded numeric typography.

accepted_units.title: Iterative generation of Gram points
accepted_units.why_material: The first stage of the SWAC pipeline converts the implicit Gram-point condition into an iterative computation over the first 5,000 indices, establishing the sampling grid on which later sign screening operates.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes project setup and the complete local description of the initial Gram-point program.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The iteration is OCR-damaged and should be scan-verified before formula-level reuse; its purpose and range are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Remainder-aware screening and local refinement of exceptional intervals
accepted_units.why_material: The computation does not treat a small approximate value as a sign: it compares magnitude with a remainder estimate, emits distinct uncertainty and proven-failure flags, then subdivides neighboring intervals to resolve exceptional behavior, exposing one case beyond the approximation's certifying power.
accepted_units.context_note: Begins with evaluation at Gram points and ends at the unresolved low maximum that motivates a fallback method.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The omitted display at lines 151-153 and damaged function symbols obscure implementation detail, but the error-control and refinement logic is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Branching from broad screening to a smaller-remainder local computation
accepted_units.why_material: One program extends broad screening while a second switches formulas for minute investigation of selected neighborhoods; the latter resolves two formerly ambiguous intervals in a way consistent with RH.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the discovery, two-program response, second ambiguous interval, and both local resolutions together.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Interval subscripts and function glyphs are OCR-corrupted, but the branch structure and resolution are readable.

accepted_units.title: Local and second-neighbor displacement of missing roots
accepted_units.why_material: The source classifies almost all Gram-law failures as compensation in an adjacent interval and isolates a smaller class where the missing root is displaced one interval farther, replacing a binary pass/fail view with spatial structure.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the convention assigning a failure to the empty interval and both directional second-neighbor patterns.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Some indices are spaced or garbled, but the taxonomy and listed directions are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Increasing failure frequency with nearly balanced displacement direction
accepted_units.why_material: The cumulative table supports the stated rise in Gram-law failure frequency through the first 10,000 intervals, while the final counts show no large imbalance between rightward and leftward displacement.
accepted_units.context_note: The uncertain-sign cases remain parenthesized rather than being silently converted into definite failures.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The table is readable from the text layer despite minor OCR typography.

accepted_units.title: Coupled Gram-law failures and three-root intervals
accepted_units.why_material: The failure events are not purely isolated: the source identifies clusters in which a three-root interval is flanked by empty intervals and gives a longer alternating root-count pattern.
accepted_units.context_note: Stops before the first figure because its curve is not represented in the extracted text.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several interval labels are OCR-damaged; the three-root/flanking-empty mechanism and the displayed root-count sequence remain recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Repeated neighboring-failure configurations
accepted_units.why_material: The prose reports that configurations like the preceding cluster recur at multiple locations and tabulates how often neighboring intervals fail together, establishing that the pattern is not unique.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the recoverable prose immediately following the extraction-defective first figure.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: One subscripted interval relation is damaged, and the link to the preceding graphical example requires the surrounding section context.

accepted_units.title: From frequency anomalies to low-amplitude extrema and close roots
accepted_units.why_material: The source explicitly changes the diagnostic target from local modulation in oscillation frequency to unusually low maxima, high minima, and nearly coincident roots, then identifies cases where ordinary sampling was insufficient and fine-mesh computation was required.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the conceptual shift, quantitative closeness criterion, case count, and escalation trigger.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Function symbols are OCR-degraded, but the amplitude-based diagnostic and fine-mesh requirement are clear.

accepted_units.title: Escalating precision to certify a nearly merged root pair
accepted_units.why_material: For cases whose extrema could not clear the Riemann-Siegel remainder bound, the computation switches to many terms of the more accurate expansion, evaluates both real and imaginary parts on a local mesh, and reports a very low maximum between two distinct roots.
accepted_units.context_note: The preceding graph is excluded; this span contains the textual method, robustness observation, figure interpretation, maximum, and root locations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact function notation and root real-part typography are damaged, while the numerical local analysis is readable; the plotted shape itself remains scan-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Prime-logarithm phase cancellation as a delicate RH stress point
accepted_units.why_material: In explicitly informal concluding comments, the author interprets the lowest observed maximum as a delicate balance among early rising and later descending terms, invokes Kronecker recurrence for repeated occurrences, and proposes targeted searches far up the strip as a possible attack.
accepted_units.context_note: Preserves the source's qualification that these are informal comments and its extrapolative language.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The sentence relating extrema to RH has an OCR defect, so only the broader prose claim about prime-logarithm relations and near-negative cancellation is safe without scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Additional 15,000-root computation
accepted_units.why_material: The proof addendum extends the reported experiment and distinguishes increasingly irregular Gram behavior from the still-observed critical-line location of all examined roots.
accepted_units.context_note: A short later update, kept separate from the main experiment's frozen first-10,000 scope.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Error bounds as routing signals for adaptive computation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Across methods, a remainder estimate is not merely a post hoc accuracy report: it determines when a sign is certifiable, when the mesh must be refined, and when the computation must switch to a more expensive representation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This synthesis is specific to the described numerical pipeline; damaged formulas prevent a formula-level reconstruction from this text layer alone.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Gram-law failure has local transport structure rather than isolated binary error
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Empty Gram intervals are usually compensated by extra roots nearby, sometimes in coupled clusters, even as their frequency increases; this makes the spatial displacement pattern more informative than the failure count alone.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The claim summarizes only the first reported interval range and does not establish a general theorem.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Rare low-amplitude extrema define the hardest certification cases
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The broad scan's most informative exceptions occur when a local extremum is too small to dominate the approximation error; these cases require a more accurate representation and motivate the author's later phase-cancellation interpretation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The phase-cancellation discussion is explicitly informal, and the observed finite examples do not validate its proposed distant-search extrapolation.
